Come to the Pedlar

William Shakespeare (1564–1616)

From “The Winter’s Tale,” Act 
IV.
 
Scene 3
W
ILL
 you buy any tape,
Or lace for your cape,
My dainty duck, my dear-a?
Any silk, any thread,
Any toys for your head,
Of the new’st and finest, finest wear-a?
Come to the pedlar;
Money’s a meddler,
That doth utter all men’s ware-a.
